anomalies.observed: The anodes of three LEDs (D25, D30, D47) sit on net /NET0189, and that net has no other connection. It has no pull-up, no supply and no driver. Their cathodes are driven through R38, R95 and R47 from the CM4 status outputs PI_nLED_Activity, Ethernet_nLED3 and Ethernet_nLED2, which are active-low.
anomalies.expected: Other active-low indicator LEDs on this board take their anode from +3V3 through a series resistor (for example D29 pin 2 on +3V3, and D20 via R15 to +3V3). The anodes of D25, D30 and D47 should be on +3V3, so the LEDs can light when the driver pulls the cathode low.
anomalies.impact: Three status LEDs (two Ethernet link/activity LEDs and the PI activity LED) would never illuminate, because their anodes have no supply path.

anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers have their isolated-side ground pins GND2 (pin 5) and GND1 (pin 4) on the same GND net. The 5V_switched_CAN side is decoupled to the same GND (C25, C79), so there is no isolation barrier between the CAN buses and the main ground.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes the CAN buses as isolated, so the GND2 side of each isolator should be a separate isolated ground, not the main GND.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation the design relies on for the CAN motor-controller buses is defeated, so ground faults and transients on the bus can couple directly into the controller ground.

parsed.summary: The netlist matches its SPICE deck, so the evidence comes from the netlist alone. The clearest deviation is that the anodes of three LEDs (D25, D30, D47) sit on a net with no supply connection, which leaves those status LEDs unable to light. A lower-confidence concern is that both isolated CAN transceivers have their isolated ground pins tied to the main GND.
